## Scott Colom is a seventh-generation Mississippian, proud husband and father of two, and district attorney who fights every day to keep Mississippians safe.
Guided by his Christian faith, Scott has dedicated his life to serving his neighbors and keeping them safe from violent criminals. Now he’s running to lower costs for families, save our Mississippi hospitals, and bring good jobs home. Scott loves his state and will always put Mississippi first – and he’ll work with anyone, Republican or Democrat, to get things done for us.
On The Issues
## Meet Scott Colom
Scott Colom is a proud seventh-generation Mississippian who’s been a prosecutor, a judge, a widely-praised District Attorney, and now a candidate for the U.S. Senate.
## Rooted In Mississippi Values
Born and raised in Columbus, Mississippi, Scott and his wife Nadia are proud parents of two (eighth-generation Mississippian) daughters. He’s the son of retired Judge Dorothy Colom – the first African-American to be elected to her region’s Chancery Court – and Wilbur Colom, an attorney and one-time Republican who worked for Ronald Reagan.
Scott is a lifelong member of Missionary Union Baptist Church in Columbus. In his spare time, Scott coaches sports and a high school mock trial team.
## Running for the US Senate – Because Mississippi Should Come First
Guided by his Christian faith and his love of Mississippi, Scott Colom announced his campaign for the U.S. Senate in September of 2025. He’s running to lower costs for families, save our Mississippi hospitals, and bring good jobs home. Our current U.S. Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith isn’t working for us anymore, voting against Mississippi jobs and investments because it serves her donors’ agenda. Scott will always put Mississippi first – and he’ll work with anyone, Republican or Democrat, to get things done for our state.
## A Reformer, Keeping Our Communities Safe
As District Attorney, Scott Colom has surged resources to prosecute violent crimes, closed a record number of cold cases, and won 94% of his trials.
Scott Colom was elected District Attorney in 2015 when, at the age of just 32, he unseated a 27-year incumbent while running on a reform platform that called for prioritizing resources to hold violent criminals accountable.
Among Scott’s successes keeping our communities safe:
- Securing convictions in over 15 high-profile murder cases.
- Bringing a predator to justice for the rape, robbery, and kidnapping of a college student at Mississippi State University, getting a sentence of 105 years in prison.
- Holding accountable a corrupt sheriff who was trading favors for sexual materials from inmates.
Scott has emphasized the importance of preventing crime by making sure criminals know they will be held accountable – and also pushing for more jobs and opportunities, which he knows is the best way to prevent crime.
Northeastern Mississippi has embraced Scott’s approach. Since first winning election to his swing district in 2015, Scott has been re-elected twice with support from Republicans, Independents and Democrats, most recently with a winning margin that exceeded national Democrats by 10 percentage points.

pages.title: Where Scott Stands - Scott Colom for Senate
pages.text:
## Where Scott Stands
District Attorney Scott Colom is a seventh-generation Mississippian, a husband, and a father of two. He is running for U.S. Senate because he believes Mississippi matters, and that the people who work hard here deserve a senator who works for them.
Scott believes a family that works hard should be able to afford groceries, gas and the light bill. Right now tariffs are taxing everything Mississippians buy, and a war nobody voted on is driving up what we pay at the pump. The Constitution gives Congress the say on both. Cindy Hyde-Smith gave Mississippi’s voice away.
In the Senate, Scott will:
- Vote to take back Congress’s power over tariffs
- Require a vote of Congress before America goes to war, because Mississippi’s service members and their families deserve that much
- Fight for a seat on the Agriculture Committee, so Mississippi farmers have a senator who actually answers to them – not Washington
Scott believes work should pay fairly. If you put in a full day, you should be able to build a life in the community where you work. But Mississippi has the lowest household income and the highest poverty rate of any state, and too many of our neighbors work full time and still come up short at the end of the month. The federal minimum wage has been $7.25 since 2009. Cindy Hyde-Smith has been in Washington for eight years, and it has not moved a penny.
In the Senate, Scott will:
- Fight to raise the minimum wage and tie it to the cost of living, so workers never wait years and years for a raise again
- Work to end the federal income tax for Mississippians making under $75,000, starting with teachers and law enforcement officers
Save our Healthcare and Hospitals
Scott believes nobody should have to choose between seeing a doctor and paying the rent, and no family should have to drive an hour to reach an emergency room. Cindy Hyde-Smith voted to cut about $11 billion from Mississippi’s Medicaid to pay for a billionaire tax break. Medicaid pays for more than half the births in this state, and eight rural hospitals are at risk of closing. She also voted against the Affordable Care Act (ACA) tax credits that kept health insurance affordable. Today 70,000 fewer Mississippians have marketplace coverage than a year ago.
In the Senate, Scott will:
- Vote to cancel the Medicaid cuts to help keep rural Mississippi’s emergency rooms and delivery rooms open
- Restore the ACA tax credits that lower insurance premiums
- Restore and strengthen eliminated federal ACA funding to incentivize Mississippi to finally expand Medicaid coverage
Make Big Tech Pay Its Own Way
Scott believes Mississippi should welcome investment, and that everybody here pays their own way, including the richest companies in the world. Data centers are already on Mississippi power bills: about $10.60 a month for the average Entergy household, according to one independent analysis. Cindy Hyde-Smith’s answer is a bill that does not make one company pay one dime. It asks states to consider it, gives them two years to think about it, and writes a voluntary pledge into law. A pledge is not protection: if a company breaks it, nothing happens and Mississippians keep paying. Meanwhile, the AI industry’s super PAC is spending to keep her in office.
In the Senate, Scott will:
- Push for a pause on new data center construction until the companies agree to pay for their own power and water, show the deal before it is signed, and hire Mississippi workers in writing
- Make sure a real person answers when AI makes decisions about our lives
- Protect the right of Mississippi communities to have the final say on whether data centers come into their communities
Clean up Washington
Scott believes public office is a trust, not a business. Washington has forgotten that. Politicians trade stocks in the industries they oversee, the biggest donors get the first call, and the well-connected get richer while everybody else pays more. Cindy Hyde-Smith is part of it. She billed more than $10,000 in Las Vegas hotels and meals to her campaign, and she takes money from fertilizer companies under federal investigation for price-fixing. Mississippi pays for it at the pump, at the pharmacy, at the co-op and at the checkout.
In the Senate, Scott will:
- Ban members of Congress, their spouses and their dependent children from trading stocks, with no loopholes
- Bar senators from taking money from companies under federal investigation
- Fund real ethics enforcement and give the Senate an ethics office with teeth
- Work to overturn Citizens United so senators answer to voters instead of donors
- Keep showing up. Scott has held more than 50 town halls. Cindy Hyde-Smith has not held a public town hall in more than six years
Keep Mississippi Safe
Scott believes everyone deserves to feel safe at home, and that nobody is above the law. He has spent ten years as a prosecutor. He won 94% of his trials, secured convictions in more than 15 high-profile murder cases and prosecuted a sheriff from his own party. Cindy Hyde-Smith voted against forcing the Epstein files into the open.
In the Senate, Scott will:
- Back law enforcement with the pay and tools to do the job
- Work to secure the border and enforce our immigration laws
- Hold the powerful to the same law as everyone else

pages.title: Scott's Anti-Corruption Plan - Scott Colom for Senate
pages.text:
## Fighting Corruption. Restoring Trust. Putting Mississippi First.
“My record as a district attorney is proof of how I make decisions: based on the evidence and the law.”
For too long, politicians in Washington have looked out for themselves, their donors and their special interests instead of the people they were elected to serve. They trade on information the public doesn’t have, hide who is funding them, and protect an unfair system that pays off for them while the cost of groceries, health care, and keeping the lights on keeps rising for the families they’re supposed to be representing. Mississippians work hard, play by the rules, and expect their leaders to do the same.
As a prosecutor, Scott Colom has spent his career holding the powerful accountable, without fear or favor and regardless of party. He investigated a sheriff in his own district who abused his office and worked with federal authorities to hold him accountable, even though the sheriff was a member of Scott’s own party. Scott learned these values from his parents—his mother, a trailblazing judge, and his father, a lawyer who has worked across party lines with Republicans and Democrats to improve Mississippi. In the Senate, he’ll bring those same values and the same standard to Washington and end corruption: following the evidence, telling the truth, and making government work for the people, not the well-connected.
## Scott's Anti-Corruption Plan:
Ban Stock Trading and Secret Crypto Profits by Members of Congress
No one should be able to use public office to get rich off information the public doesn’t have.
Scott supports a full ban on stock trading by members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children, requiring them to divest or move their holdings into a blind trust, with real-time public disclosure so voters can see whose interests they’re protecting.
And the rules have to keep up with how the self-dealing is actually happening right now. No official, however powerful, should be able to launch or promote their own cryptocurrency, take in money from foreign or anonymous buyers, and pocket the profits while setting the policies that make that coin worth more. That is the opposite of investing; it’s selling access to the highest bidder, often to buyers we can’t even see. When the people writing the rules are cashing in on them, the ones who lose are the Mississippians who just want their government to work for them.
Public service should never be a pathway to personal enrichment.
Strengthen Ethics Enforcement
Ethics rules only matter if they’re enforced.
Scott will support stronger independent oversight of Congress and tougher penalties for ethics violations, including fully funding the independent watchdog that polices Congress and giving the Senate its own ethics office with real power to act. When there are no consequences for selling out the people you serve, nothing stops a senator from doing it again, and it’s working families who keep paying for a Washington that answers to everyone but them.
Crack Down on Corruption and Public Fraud
Whether corruption happens in Washington or a county courthouse, it should be investigated and prosecuted without fear or favor.
Scott has done it. As district attorney, he uncovered corruption inside a local sheriff’s office and brought in federal investigators to hold those responsible accountable, because the law has to apply to the powerful, not just the powerless. In the Senate, he’ll fight to give federal anti-corruption investigators the resources they need, protect the whistleblowers who expose wrongdoing, and crack down on the fraud that drains the federal programs Mississippians count on, from health care to disaster relief. And he believes a senator has no business taking money from companies under federal investigation while the families back home pay the price.
Some folks in Washington talk about corruption. Scott has actually done something about it.
Will Fight to Overturn Citizens United
The Supreme Court’s decision in Citizens United opened the floodgates for unlimited special interest spending in our elections, giving wealthy donors and outside groups far too much influence over who gets elected and what happens once they’re in office. Mississippians deserve a government that answers to voters, not the biggest checkbooks.
Scott believes our campaign finance system is broken, and he’ll work with Democrats, Republicans, and Independents to overturn Citizens United and restore the power of everyday Americans in our democracy. Scott also supports reforms that increase transparency, strengthen disclosure of campaign spending and lobbying, and make it easier for voters to know who is trying to influence their elected officials.
Scott Colom has spent his career enforcing the law, not making excuses for people who break it. His parents raised him to believe the rules apply to everyone, whether you’re a violent criminal, a powerful corporation, or a member of Congress, and that the law should protect the innocent as fiercely as it holds the guilty to account.
While career politicians protect the unfair system that rewards them, Scott has spent his career holding people accountable when they abuse it, regardless of party.
The people of Mississippi deserve a government that works for them, not the wealthy, the well-connected, or the insiders who profit while working families pay more. Scott will fight to end the self-dealing, bring hidden influence into the open, and make sure public office is about serving the public.
Because in Mississippi, no one should be above the law, and no one should be beneath its protection.
If you’re like Scott and believe it’s time to root out the corruption in Washington that’s costing Mississippians more, text SCOTT to 54937 and join our movement!

pages.title: WATCH: Prosecutor Scott Colom Lays Out His Plan to Clean Up Washington, Brings the Receipts on Cindy Hyde-Smith's Corruption - Scott Colom for Senate
pages.text:
July 14, 2026
## “Corruption Costs Mississippi”: Read District Attorney Colom’s full Anti-Corruption Agenda — MORE HERE
Columbus, MS — Today, standing outside the Lowndes County Courthouse where he has served as district attorney for a decade, Scott Colom unveiled his agenda to root out corruption in Washington and made a prosecutor’s case against Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith’s role in Washington’s corruption, laying out the receipts on her self-dealing, illustrating how each one connects to a cost to Mississippians, and highlighting his own record of holding the powerful accountable regardless of party. Introduced by his mentor, Pastor and Attorney Orlando Richmond, Colom leveled a simple charge: Cindy Hyde-Smith went to Washington and started working for herself, and Mississippi pays the bill.
“Cindy Hyde-Smith went to Washington and started working for herself. She collected checks from rich people to pay for her own luxury living, and when a bill came up that would have made her explain it, she voted no. The farmers got the bill. She got the donation. I’ve spent my career as a prosecutor holding the powerful accountable, without fear or favor and no matter their party, and that’s exactly what I’ll bring to Washington,” said District Attorney Scott Colom.
In remarks to press, flanked by supporters, Colom unveiled a four-part plan to root out the corruption costing Mississippians:
- Ban stock trading and secret crypto profits : Bar members of Congress, their spouses, and their children from trading stocks or cashing in on secret crypto deals in the industries they regulate, with full divestment and real-time disclosure. And bar any public official, however powerful, from launching or promoting their own cryptocurrency, taking money from foreign or anonymous buyers, and pocketing the profits while setting the policies that make that coin worth more.
- Strengthen ethics enforcement : Back independent watchdogs with real teeth and a Senate ethics office with the power to act, so breaking the rules finally comes with consequences.
- Crack down on corruption and public fraud : Give federal investigators the resources to follow the money, protect the whistleblowers who expose wrongdoing, and root out fraud wherever it hides, from Washington to the local services Mississippians count on.
- Get big money out of politics : Work across party lines to overturn Citizens United and put voters, not the biggest checkbooks, back in charge of our elections.
Colom built the case for that plan on Hyde-Smith’s own record. She billed more than $10,000 in Las Vegas hotel stays to her campaign, funded by lobbyist and corporate money, then voted to block the transparency measure that would have required her to explain it. She has taken checks from fertilizer companies under federal investigation for price-fixing, gouging the very farmers she claims to fight for on one of their biggest expenses. She voted to block a ban on members of Congress trading the stocks they regulate. And she voted to give the crypto industry the green light without the one safeguard that would have barred the president from cashing in, as he pocketed more than $1.4 billion in crypto income in a single year. Each receipt, Colom argued, lands on a cost: farmers pay more at the co-op, families pay more at the checkout, and billionaires in New York and California got a tax handout while Mississippian’s premiums climb and rural hospitals hang on.
He grounded the case in his own record. As district attorney, Colom investigated a sheriff in his own district who was preying on a woman in his jail, brought in federal investigators, and held him accountable, even though the sheriff was a member of his own party. “That is the difference between talking and doing,” Colom added.
